red_flags.name: Complete inability to urinate (acute urinary retention) — no output despite urge
Anuria in the setting of known trauma
Haematuria with clots, severe flank/back pain, or fever (obstructing clot, stone with infection, or tumour)
Haematuria with unintentional weight loss or age >40 (red flag for urological malignancy)
Dysuria with high fever, rigors, flank pain, nausea/vomiting (suspected pyelonephritis or urosepsis)
Hypertensive urgency: BP ≥180/120 mmHg with new headache, visual change, or confusion
Foamy urine with progressive leg/facial oedema (suspected nephrotic syndrome)
Pneumaturia (gas in urine stream) — suggests colovesical fistula, needs urgent surgical review
New urinary incontinence following trauma or spinal injury
Poor stream / dribbling with perineal pain and fever in a male (suspected prostate abscess)
Foamy urine in pregnancy with headache or hypertension (suspected pre-eclampsia)
Oliguria or anuria with confusion, severe oedema, or absent urine output >12h (acute kidney injury / renal failure)
Dysuria with painless penile/vaginal discharge and sexual exposure (STI — chlamydia, trichomonal, candidal)
Bladder pain with gross haematuria (interstitial cystitis with bleeding)
